source_text: Baptisma quoque, inquiunt, non vere homines novos facere asserunt, id est, non plenam dare remissionem peccatorum, sed ex parte filios Dei fieri, ex parte autem saeculi filios, id est, diaboli, remanere
pass_a_gloss: Baptism also, they say, they assert does not truly make human beings new: that is, does not give full remission of sins, but that they become in part sons of God, yet remain in part sons of the age, that is, of the devil.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: They also claim that baptism does not truly make people new: that is, that it does not grant full remission of sins. They insist that people become partly children of God but remain partly children of this world—that is, of the devil. (Luke 20:34; possible further echo: 1 John 3:10.)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
